title: Le Verrier (1846), Table n° 77: 279 observations of Uranus, 1690–1845, transcribed and reconciled
description:
Transcription of Table n° 77 of U. J. Le Verrier, Recherches sur les mouvements de la planète Herschel (dite Uranus), Connaissance des Temps pour l'an 1849, Additions, pp. 129–136 (Paris, 1846). This is the table of 279 observed apparent right ascensions and declinations of Uranus, 1690–1845, that Le Verrier compared with the theory of his day before predicting Neptune. Beside each observation it gives his computed values and his computed-minus-observed residuals in RA, Dec, geocentric longitude and latitude.

Every cell is kept exactly as printed. The package contains:

  • the reconciled table;
  • the two independent transcription passes, from two scans of the 1846 offprint;
  • the resolution log for their 14 disagreements, each resolved against a third printing (BnF Gallica);
  • a table of 7 misprints in the source, each with an argument from the table itself;
  • two spot-check records of the same 28 rows (336 cells): one by an AI model, one by a human;
  • a derived file of 529 measurements in degrees with Julian Dates and observatories;
  • a data dictionary and a Frictionless Data Package descriptor.

The transcription and the reconciliation were done by an AI model, not by an independent human. The dataset was then spot-checked by a human against the Gallica scan (28 rows, 336 cells, 0 discrepancies). The human check was done by the dataset author, and the other 251 rows have had no human check. See README.md for the method and its limitations.
notes: Transcription, reconciliation and a first spot check by an AI model under the direction of the creator. Then spot-checked by a human against the Gallica scan (28 rows, 336 cells, 0 discrepancies), by the creator. The 1846 source is in the public domain; the page scans used are not redistributed (URLs and SHA-256 hashes in MANIFEST.md).
references: Le Verrier, U. J. (1846). Recherches sur les mouvements de la planète Herschel (dite Uranus). Connaissance des Temps pour l'an 1849, Additions, 3–254. Paris: Bachelier.
